paper.title_en: Spinning compact object and chaos in galactic centres
paper.abstract_en: Galactic centres are extremely complex environments, consisting primarily of a supermassive black hole (SMBH) surrounded by asymmetric mass distributions such as nuclear star clusters (NSC) and molecular gas, which form disks or halos. Together these components exert a gravitational field which, combined with relativistic corrections from the spin of the SMBH, generates strongly nonlinear dynamics and chaotic orbits. We model this region using a multipolar expansion potential, in which the central compact object is represented by the Artemova-Björnsson-Novikov pseudo-Newtonian potential, which mimics the spin dependence of a Kerr-like BH. The surrounding halo is modelled as an axisymmetric, shell-like mass distribution expanded to dipole order to induce asymmetry. Previous works have mostly quantified the chaos caused by the BH spin and dipole moment using Poincaré sections, SALI and other chaos indicators. In this study, we incorporate stability analysis and Newton-Raphson basins of convergence to provide a global view of the dynamics of the system. Stability analysis around fixed points gives deeper insight into the local behaviour, while basins of convergence show sensitivity to initial conditions and reveal fractal boundaries. Our results show that the BH spin substantially reshapes the equilibrium landscape. Depending on its magnitude, it can either intensify the chaos induced by the halo asymmetry or simplify the phase space. These results improve our understanding of how relativistic spin effects and multipole moments collectively affect particle motion in galactic centres.
